Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the second innings. The two umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed by the Indians who spread across the field. Gaby Lewis and Sarah Forbes, the Irish openers stride out with their eyes set on providing a strong platform for the side. Titas Sadhu has the new ball and will start the proceedings. Away we go!
... The Run Chase ...

A mammoth chase awaits Ireland as they prepare to take on India's formidable total. While India's bowling showed some vulnerability in the middle overs during the first ODI, the cushion of a massive score should allow their bowlers to operate with greater freedom. However, this isn't going to be a straightforward task - Ireland's batting lineup boasts some seasoned campaigners who'll be eager to test India's relatively green bowling attack. We will back with the run chase in a few minutes. Do not go anywhere!

Jemimah Rodrigues is up for a flash interview! She says the ton means a lot to her. Adds that she is glad that the team has given the role to bat at 4 and she could deliver for the side. Mentions that her target was to be out there till the 50th over and she knew a 100 would be on the cards for her if she did that. Reckons that she initially took a bit of time and accelerated when it was needed. Closes by saying they can not afford to take any team lightly and they have seen teams chase even 390 in the domestic circuit so they will not get complacent.

India was already looking for something in excess of 300-ish but this injection of momentum further increased the chances. With the wickets in hand, the two really stepped on the gas in the last ten and took the wings out of the sails of the Irish bowlers. Harleen though missed out on her century, but ensured that India leapfrogged and went beyond 350. As a result, India garnered 102 runs in the last ten overs with Jemimah Rodrigues notching up her maiden ODI ton.

Call it inexperience from the bowlers, or the pitch just flattening up further, Ireland couldn't capitalize on that double breakthrough as Harleen and Jemimah steadily built another substantial partnership in the middle overs. What started as careful accumulation soon transformed into an aggressive batting display, with both batters finding the fence with regularity. They picked their moments wisely by defending the good deliveries while ensuring the loose ones didn't go unpunished.

With two new batters at the crease, Ireland tried to press the opposition as Harleen and Jemimah were just getting their eyes settled. Dempsey and Canning did bowl better spells with more discipline and didn't allow the two to score freely. The scoring rate slowed down a bit with boundaries dried up for nearly five overs. But it was still above run-a-ball, helped well by the openers. Hence, India mustered up 41 runs in the next set of ten overs, but without losing any wickets.

The scoring rate accelerated further after the powerplay with both playing percentage cricket with minimal risk-taking. Smriti reached her half-century, and both also survived on a dropped chance along the way. Pratika soon followed with her own fifty, and together they achieved a centurion partnership.  However, the momentum shifted a bit to Ireland when Georgina Dempsey made amends for earlier fielding lapses by catching Smriti first. She then followed it up and struck again with her very first delivery, dismissing Pratika. Within a snap, India lost both their openers, getting reduced from 156/0 to 156/2.

India Women got off to a methodical start on a batting-friendly pitch, with openers Smriti and Pratika adopting a measured approach. The pair skillfully found gaps in the field and maintained consistent strike rotation. Ireland's bowlers struggled early on, failing to capitalize on any new ball movement and showing inconsistent line and length. Once settled, both batters shifted gears smoothly. Pratika looked increasingly confident with each stroke, while Smriti showed her class, threading the ball through gaps almost at will. The powerplay yielded a handsome 75 runs without loss, helped along by some shaky Irish fielding that was a far cry from their sharp performance in the first ODI.
A job well done with the bat by India as they have posted a mountainous total of 370 on the board, breaching their previous highest of 357 against the same opposition in Potchefstroom back in 2017.
